title: Affine perfect extension after adjoining a finite locally free summand
statement: Let X be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme] and U a quasi-compact open subscheme of X. For every perfect object F of D(\mathcal O_U) [def-pc-derived-category, def-pc-perfect-complex], there exist an integer r and a finite locally free \mathcal O_U-module \mathcal F such that \mathcal F[-r] \oplus F is isomorphic on U to the restriction of a perfect object of D(\mathcal O_X).

proof.text: Use [lem-pc-strictly-perfect-finite-free-refinement] on each perfect local model and forget its lower bound. This proves pseudo-coherence directly. Apply [lem-sc-affine-pseudo-coherent-lift] to obtain a bounded-above finite-free sheaf complex K on X and an isomorphism of its restriction with F.

The open U is quasi-compact by hypothesis and quasi-separated as an open of an affine scheme. Apply [lem-sc-perfect-ext-bounded-qcoh-vanishing] to F to get a cohomology gap [a,b]. Apply [lem-sc-affine-perfect-low-truncation-triangle] to the supplied K and its representation of F to obtain N and the low triangles. Choose r=min(N,a), so r<=N and r-1<a, and obtain a finite locally free M, perfect P on X, and triangle M[-r] -> P|U -> F -> M[1-r].

A finite locally free sheaf is quasi-coherent. A single complex on such a sheaf is in D_QCoh: its cohomology is M in its single degree and zero elsewhere. The shift isomorphism identifies M[1-r] with the single complex in degree r-1, which is strictly below a. Its cohomology vanishes throughout [a,b]. Hence the gap theorem makes Hom(F,M[1-r]) a subsingleton and the triangle third map is zero.

Apply [lem-pc-derived-zero-third-split], Mathlib exists_iso_binaryBiproduct_of_distTriang, to this distinguished triangle. It gives P|U isomorphic to the biproduct of the single complex M in degree r and F. The single functor shift isomorphism identifies the first term with M[0][-r]; map this isomorphism through the biproduct and use the witnesses r,M,P.
